objectives.description: Add land verb: specs/** refusal before any merge, otherwise git merge --no-ff
Merge-conflict handling: abort, preserve branch/worktree, named conflict verdict, distinct exit code
Dirty-overlap refusal against main-tree uncommitted modifications
JSON verdict on stdout for every outcome; all diagnostics on stderr (JSON-channel discipline)
Extend test-dispatch-worktree.sh with land cases (clean, specs refusal, conflict, dirty-overlap, nothing-to-land) plus two bonus cases

approaches_tried.approach: same-line conflict fixture (both sides editing one pre-existing shared line)
approaches_tried.reason: an add/add conflict (both sides independently adding the same new filename with different content after the branch forked) reproduces a genuine, unresolvable git conflict just as validly and needed less fixture setup; used that instead of pre-seeding shared content.

deviations.description: Added a PROJECT_ROOT-resolves-inside-a-worktree refusal to land (verdict=unavailable, exit 93) beyond the plan's stated task list
deviations.reason: The plan's Phase 5 tasks did not explicitly call for this guard, but land's own header/design already documents 'run from the main tree' as a hard requirement (inherited from Phase 4's provision, which the plan's own header commentary flags as load-bearing for the specs/** refusal to make sense at all). Without the guard, invoking the worktree's own hardlinked copy of the script would silently merge into the wrong tree. Recorded as a deliberate strengthening, not scope creep beyond the phase's own goal.
